subject: Decision Making
title: Autonomous Vehicles and Split-Second Choices
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Autonomous Vehicles and Split-Second Choices.

hook.text: A self-driving car must choose in milliseconds: swerve into a wall or hit a pedestrian. Who programmed that decision?

buildup.text: The trolley problem is no longer a thought experiment. Autonomous vehicles face real-world versions thousands of times.

discovery.text: MIT's Moral Machine surveyed 40 million people. Preferences varied wildly across cultures.

twist.text: Most AV accidents are mundane: misjudging a turn, misreading a stop sign.

climax.text: Self-driving cars will save millions of lives. But every algorithm failure will be judged as a moral choice.

punchline.text: The trolley problem is now real code. No culture agrees on the answer.

quiz.question: What did MIT's Moral Machine survey reveal?
options: Moral preferences for autonomous vehicle decisions vary significantly across cultures
